entry.title: AlphaFold-Multimer predicts 2,895 interactions among human mitochondrial proteins
entry.summary: Texas A&M AgriLife Research screened 630,003 protein pairs from about 1,100 human mitochondrial proteins with AlphaFold-Multimer and identified 2,895 likely interactions, more than half not previously reported, giving 85 uncharacterized proteins their first probable partners. The paper appeared in… (Discovery - Texas A&M AgriLife Research and Washington University School of Medicine in St. Louis; announced 2026-11-05)

entry.title: Collaborating LLM agents propose and test a calibration rule for diamond quantum spins
entry.summary: Mutually reviewing LLM agents selected a question about the minimum number of calibration settings needed to predict responses to microwave pulse sequences in diamond spin ensembles, derived the theory and tested it experimentally. The first measurement was inconclusive because of signal drift… (Discovery - Institute of Science Tokyo; announced 2026-10-29)

entry.title: Quine ranks compounds that shift pancreatic cancer cells toward a basal state
entry.summary: Microsoft's Quine, a multimodal biology world model, prioritized thousands of compounds for shifting tumor cell states, and a handful were tested in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma cell lines. The top-ranked compounds produced the largest classical-to-basal shifts, as validated by wet-lab… (Discovery - Microsoft Research; Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT; announced 2026-09-29)

entry.title: YOLO detector tracks endangered European hamster activity in camera traps
entry.summary: A YOLO object-detection model trained on 2023 camera-trap videos detected European hamsters with an F1-score of 0.93 and accuracy of 0.93. Its activity profile matched human annotation and showed peak activity at dusk and a secondary peak before sunrise. The evidence covers one season at one… (Discovery - Goethe University Frankfurt; announced 2026-09-04)

entry.title: AI designs physics experiments that outperform human-designed setups
entry.summary: Krenn group (Tübingen, TU Wien and collaborators) treats experiment design as an optimisation problem, using physics simulations to propose and refine setups that yield more precise measurements than human designs across several physics areas. The institutional announcements give no quantitative… (Discovery - University of Tübingen; TU Wien; University of Vienna; announced 2026-09-02)

entry.title: Global methane point sources mapped from EMIT imaging spectroscopy with a vision transformer
entry.summary: The MAPL-EMIT vision transformer uses full EMIT radiance spectra to jointly retrieve methane enhancements, plume outlines and source locations across global scenes, trained on 3.6 million synthetic plumes. The paper reports high recall and precision and better detection of weak plumes than… (Discovery - Google Research; Carnegie Institution for Science; Jet Propulsion Laboratory, California Institute of Technology; announced 2026-09-01)

entry.title: FluEmbed predicts H3N2 antigenic drift from sequence alone
entry.summary: FluEmbed, a protein language model framework, predicted influenza A (H3N2) antigenicity from RNA sequence with Spearman correlations of 0.67 to 0.80 against hemagglutination inhibition titers. It outperformed Hamming, BLOSUM62 and phylogenetic baselines, and in-silico mutagenesis showed… (Discovery - University of Georgia; announced 2026-08-11)

entry.title: Quake Neural Operator builds microseismic catalogues without phase picking
entry.summary: The Quake Neural Operator detects and locates microseismic events directly from continuous data without explicit phase picking. Applied to the Geysers geothermal field, it finds nearly an order of magnitude more seismic detections than routine catalogues, checked against the Phase Neural Operator… (Discovery - University of Texas at El Paso, Department of Earth, Environmental and Resource Sciences; announced 2026-07-06)

entry.title: BirdNET embeddings distinguish individual North Atlantic right whales
entry.summary: Audio embeddings from the BirdNET model robustly distinguished individual North Atlantic right whales in upcall recordings from 234 samples across 11 individuals at 3 sites. Simulations showed that an extra 7 dB or more of signal excess is needed to identify individuals under ambient noise. The… (Discovery - Cornell K. Lisa Yang Center for Conservation Bioacoustics; Oregon State University; Syracuse University; announced 2026-06-30)

entry.title: A Herculaneum scroll read end to end without opening
entry.summary: Machine-learning ink detection on synchrotron scans let papyrologists read about 22 columns of a likely Stoic ethics text from scroll PHerc. 1667. The text is fragmentary because only the inner core survives, and humans transcribed and reviewed every reading. (Discovery - Vesuvius Challenge, EduceLab and ESRF; announced 2026-06-25)

entry.title: Machine learning pre-screening finds kagome superconductors YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2
entry.summary: A machine-learning pre-screen of candidate compounds, followed by first-principles calculations, selected YRu3B2 and LuRu3B2, which were measured as bulk superconductors with Tc of 0.81 K and 0.95 K and near 100% superconducting volume fraction. Evidence caveat: these are low-temperature… (Discovery - Aalto University; Rice University; Princeton University; announced 2026-06-17)

entry.title: Satellite model maps collapse and surviving Acropora corals in Belize
entry.summary: A supervised Random Tree classifier on satellite images predicted a drop of over 90% in live Acropora cover at Belize from 2011 to 2023 across 25 km². Field searches in June 2025 found live or recently dead colonies at 28 of 42 predicted sites and live colonies at 16 previously undocumented… (Discovery - Washington and Lee University; Macalester College; announced 2026-06-02)

entry.title: Deep learning finds multimetallic single-atom catalysts across material families
entry.summary: The Crossbreeding Neural Network (CBNN), trained jointly on carbon-supported single-atom catalysts and perovskite oxides, screened 8,008 candidates. Its top W-Mo-Ru-Rh design on a perovskite support outperformed the comparison catalysts in synthesis and electrochemical tests, and the 12 predicted… (Discovery - Institute for Basic Science (IBS) Center for Nanoparticle Research; Seoul National University; announced 2026-05-28)

entry.title: AI-driven formal proof search resolves Erdős problems and OEIS conjectures
entry.summary: An agent that alternates LLM proof generation with Lean verification autonomously resolved 9 of 353 open Erdős problems and proved 44 of 492 OEIS conjectures, at a cost of a few hundred dollars per problem according to the abstract. Proofs are Lean-verified, so the checking is mechanical; the… (Discovery - Google DeepMind; announced 2026-05-21)

entry.title: Empirical Research Assistance writes expert-level scientific code across six domains
entry.summary: Google's Empirical Research Assistance (ERA), a Gemini-based tree-search system, reaches expert-level performance on six benchmarks spanning genomics, public health, satellite imagery, neuroscience, time-series forecasting and mathematics. Its state-level U.S. hospital admission forecasts for flu… (Discovery - Google Research; announced 2026-05-19)

entry.title: Machine learning designs bulk metallic glasses with about 2,450 HV hardness
entry.summary: Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials used VIBANN, an attention-based variational network trained on only 673 compositions, to design hard multicomponent bulk metallic glasses. Five alloys were synthesised as fully amorphous 2 mm rods, reaching about 2,450 HV, with high-energy X-ray… (Discovery - Max Planck Institute for Sustainable Materials; announced 2026-05-12)

entry.title: PoLARIS: a self-driving microfluidic lab finds brighter lead-free perovskite nanoplatelets
entry.summary: A closed-loop microfluidic platform ran 120 experiments in one 12-hour campaign on double perovskite nanoplatelets with up to six elements and identified the brightest lead-free composition found in that campaign. The press release gives no numerical photoluminescence gain, so the improvement is… (Discovery - North Carolina State University; Brown University; announced 2026-05-04)

entry.title: A designed generalist binding protein evolves into a highly active designed enzyme
entry.summary: Crystallographic fragment screening found weak binders of a designed protein, which were then evolved into a catalyst that the authors describe as the most active designed enzyme to date. AI models were used in the redesign step, while the crystal structures and enzyme assays were experimental.… (Discovery - University of California, San Francisco (Fraser and DeGrado groups); announced 2026-05-04)

entry.title: New Zarankiewicz numbers and bounds from OpenEvolve search
entry.summary: Using the open-source OpenEvolve LLM-driven evolutionary framework with a custom reward, the authors find exact values Z(11,21,3,3)=116, Z(11,22,3,3)=121 and Z(12,22,3,3)=132, and lower bounds for 41 further parameter sets, at under $30 per case. entry.title: Qiushi Discovery Engine proposes and validates an optical bilinear interaction
entry.summary: An LLM agent (Qiushi Discovery Engine) given only the topic optical computing for AI ran an open-ended study of 145.9 million tokens, 3,242 LLM calls and 1,242 tool calls, and proposed an optical bilinear interaction analogous to the attention operation in Transformers, which the authors say they… (Discovery - Zhejiang University; announced 2026-04-29)

entry.title: Simulated training data locates archaeological tar-kiln-like sites in Louisiana, field check finds WWII features
entry.summary: Machine learning models trained on simulated landscape data flagged 9 of 12 known targets (model 1) and all 12 (model 2, with 686 false positives among 709 remaining predictions) in Kisatchie National Forest, Louisiana; a model trained on real South Carolina tar kilns found 11 of 12. Field visits… (Discovery - University of New Mexico; New Mexico Consortium; Utah State University; Louisiana State University; announced 2026-04-27)

entry.title: Gauss completes the Lean formalization of the dimension-8 sphere packing proof
entry.summary: Math Inc's autoformalization model Gauss completed the final stages of the Lean verification of Viazovska's proof that the E8 lattice is the optimal sphere packing in dimension 8, working with the human formalization team. The paper describes the human-AI collaboration and the verification in the… (Discovery - Math Inc; Hariharan, Viazovska and collaborators; announced 2026-04-25)

entry.title: An LLM agent in an air-free robotic lab maps lithium halide spinel conductors
entry.summary: An agent-guided self-driving lab ran 352 air-sensitive synthesis samples, realizing 72% of the 171 pairwise combinations of 19 metals. The share of samples meeting both ionic conductivity above 0.05 mS/cm and high spinel phase purity rose from 1.33% in the first 75 agent-proposed samples to 5.33%… (Discovery - Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory and University of California, Berkeley; announced 2026-04-13)

entry.title: Claude-assisted discovery of an Apache ActiveMQ Classic code-injection flaw
entry.summary: Horizon3.ai reports a remote code execution flaw in ActiveMQ Classic, introduced about 13 years earlier, that chains the Jolokia management API with network-connector VM transports. Apache rates it important and fixes it in 5.19.4 and 6.2.3. (Vulnerability - Horizon3.ai and Apache ActiveMQ; announced 2026-04-07)

entry.title: Anderson's 2014 commutative algebra problem resolved by Rethlas and Archon
entry.summary: An informal reasoning agent (Rethlas) and a formal verification agent (Archon) resolve an open problem in commutative algebra posed by D. D. Anderson in 2014, as a counterexample. The Lean 4 formalization has about 19,450 lines and was produced in roughly 80 agent hours, with the code public on… (Discovery - Peking University; Westlake University; Kyoto University; Tianjin University; announced 2026-04-04)

entry.title: Erdős Problem #650 solved with ChatGPT strategy and Aristotle Lean proof
entry.summary: The authors prove f(m) = min(m, ceil(2 sqrt(m))) for all m, resolving Erdős Problem #650 on Bloom's site, where f(m) counts disjoint divisibility pairs in an interval for an m-element set. The detailed argument was formally verified in Lean by Harmonic's Aristotle, following a strategy proposed by… (Discovery - Southeast University; Xi'an Jiaotong University; announced 2026-03-30)

entry.title: AI-designed protein family binds and senses small molecules, including cortisol
entry.summary: Designed binding proteins for six small-molecule classes, built on a deep-learning NTF2-like fold, were experimentally characterised; one was turned into a cortisol biosensor. Sensitivity reported earlier as nanomolar in the 2023 preprint; the 2026 peer-reviewed version is the source of record.… (Discovery - KAIST; University of Washington Institute for Protein Design; announced 2026-03-28)

entry.title: Catalysis AI Agent derives design rules for copper single-atom alloys for CO2 electroreduction
entry.summary: An LLM-based Catalysis AI Agent identified an energy descriptor for classifying copper-based single-atom alloys and a structural descriptor for predicting activation energy. The team reports experimental testing and that the approach extends to other metal dopants. Evidence caveat: the press… (Discovery - Tohoku University, Advanced Institute for Materials Research (AIMR); announced 2026-03-26)

entry.title: Claude finds a FreeBSD RPCSEC_GSS kernel stack overflow
entry.summary: FreeBSD advisory SA-26:08 describes a stack overflow in the RPCSEC_GSS code that can allow remote code execution in the kernel, with no workaround, affecting all supported versions. It credits Nicholas Carlini using Claude, Anthropic. (Vulnerability - Anthropic and FreeBSD Project; announced 2026-03-26)

entry.title: RAVEN pipeline validates 118 new TESS planets and vets over 2,000 candidates
entry.summary: A pipeline combining box least squares detection with machine-learning classifiers, trained on realistic simulations, searched 2.2 million TESS main-sequence stars in full-frame images (sectors 1 to 55). It newly validates 118 planets, 31 of them newly detected, and vets over 2,000 candidates… (Discovery - Warwick University and collaborators; announced 2026-03-23)

entry.title: Adaptive AI experiment planning finds multi-promoter catalysts in under 50 experiments
entry.summary: Fritz Haber Institute, with BASF and BasCat, used adaptive experiment planning in a self-driving lab to search over 10^13 promoter combinations with fewer than 50 experiments. The method was validated on propane-to-propylene conversion, and the authors report synergistic promoter effects that… (Discovery - Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society; BASF; BasCat (UniCat BASF JointLab); announced 2026-03-19)

entry.title: ChatHEA assistant guides high-entropy alloy catalysts for fuel cells
entry.summary: ChatHEA, a domain-specific LLM assistant for high-entropy alloy electrocatalysis, guided synthesis and screening of 100 five-element alloy catalysts. The FeCoCuPtIr catalyst reached a peak power density of 0.789 W cm-2 in a fuel cell and outperformed commercial Pt/C in electrochemical tests.… (Discovery - Tohoku University, Advanced Institute for Materials Research (AIMR); announced 2026-03-14)

entry.title: AlphaEvolve raises nine Ramsey lower bounds
entry.summary: AlphaEvolve-generated search algorithms improved bounds such as R(3,13) from 60 to 61, R(4,16) from 170 to 174 and R(4,19) from 213 to 219. The paper does not describe independent verification; search code is public. arXiv preprint, latest version read. (Discovery - Google DeepMind and academic co-authors; announced 2026-03-10)

entry.title: Claude's Cycles: a Hamiltonian cycle decomposition found by Claude
entry.summary: Knuth's note reports that Claude Opus 4.6 found an explicit decomposition of the arcs of the m^3-vertex digraph into three directed Hamiltonian cycles for odd m, an open problem Knuth posed. Knuth's proof of the construction was reportedly formally verified in Lean by Kim Morrison. Caveat: sources… (Discovery - Stanford University; Anthropic; announced 2026-02-28)

entry.title: LFAST: an LLM agent drives robotic synthesis of the new COF-2000 framework
entry.summary: A GPT-4o-based agent (LFAST) screened reaction conditions over a 96-condition matrix and refined them after each round, raising the crystallinity index of a reference covalent organic framework by 350% and yielding COF-2000, a previously unreported material with higher structural order. The… (Discovery - University of California, Berkeley (Yaghi group); announced 2026-02-23)

entry.title: De novo designed proteins modulate GPCR signalling in the dopamine D1 receptor
entry.summary: Zhejiang University designed four de novo GPCR exoframe modulators (GEMs) that target the transmembrane domain of the dopamine D1 receptor. Functional assays showed they act as positive, negative or biased allosteric modulators, and one restored activity in loss-of-function receptor mutants.… (Discovery - Zhejiang University; announced 2026-02-16)

entry.title: Hacktron's AI agent finds a BeyondTrust remote-support command injection
entry.summary: Hacktron reports an OS command injection in BeyondTrust Remote Support and Privileged Remote Access, rated critical with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.9 and a variant of CVE-2024-12356 on the same WebSocket endpoint. BeyondTrust published advisory BT26-02 on 6 February 2026. (Vulnerability - Hacktron AI and BeyondTrust; announced 2026-02-06)

entry.title: First-principles neural network finds crystallization of fractional quantum Hall liquids
entry.summary: A self-attention neural-network wavefunction (MagNet), trained only by minimising the microscopic Hamiltonian of interacting electrons in a magnetic field, finds both topological liquid and electron-crystal ground states across a range of Landau-level mixing. The authors present it as a method… (Discovery - MIT; announced 2026-02-03)

entry.title: Co-FunSearch finds adversarial instances raising the Best-Fit bin packing bound
entry.summary: A human-LLM pipeline (Co-FunSearch) finds adversarial instances for heuristics, raising the lower bound for Best-Fit bin packing in the random-order model from 1.3 to 1.5. The authors prove the 3/2 ratio analytically and report a search-found instance scoring 1.497 over 10,000 random shuffles… (Discovery - University of Bonn; Google DeepMind; University of Manitoba; announced 2026-01-23)

entry.title: Erdős Problem #728 solved with GPT-5.2 Pro and Aristotle
entry.summary: GPT-5.2 Pro produced the argument and Harmonic's Aristotle a Lean proof of infinitely many triples with a logarithmic gap in a factorial divisibility condition. The arXiv writeup calls it resolved autonomously, which is the author's claim; no independent review is stated. (Discovery - OpenAI and Harmonic; announced 2026-01-12)
